subject: Planning: POC working session + routing tier playtest

Subject: POC kickoff & hands-on working session (routing + load test)

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightCommerce is excited to move to a short POC to validate routing tiers and fallback behavior under realistic traffic. We'd like a hands-on session that covers:

- Prompt review and a few representative traffic patterns (catalog lookups, long chat sessions)
- Model selection and fallback rules (latency vs quality tradeoffs)
- A light load test to exercise batching and KV caching behavior

Would you be able to run a 90-minute working session next week? Our core team: me (ops), Elena Ruiz (platform lead) and two engineers. We can do the mornings PT on 5/19 or 5/20.

Also, please send any prework so we can align prompts and traffic samples.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering, BrightCommerce

Adding a couple of specifics to help Samir prep: 

Quick agenda suggestion (90m):
1) 10m — intros & success criteria (BrightCommerce ops)
2) 20m — prompt review + sample traffic mapping (we'll use your CSV)
3) 30m — routing tier walkthrough (model variants, quantization recommendations, fallback rules)
4) 20m — live load test & observation (we'll throttle/scale to simulate spikes)
5) 10m — next steps (rollout plan, evaluation metrics)

On model selection: we'll bring two model variants for the demo — a lower-cost quantized variant and a higher-quality fp16 variant. Fallback policy we'll propose: prefer same-region lower-cost variant within 150ms; if above 150ms or token budget exceeded, failover to cross-region high-throughput instance with degraded generation length cap.

I'll prepare the short slides and a one-page fallback matrix for the session.

— Laura
Product Manager, Redwood Console

Samir — thanks for the sample. We can do the 11:30 PT slot on 2027-05-19 and will place the load test in the last 25 minutes as requested. 

To clarify infra for the test:
- We'll run on our Dedicated lab but emulate the lower-cost quantized variant and a throttled lower-tier using scheduling policies. This reproduces latency & failover without requiring a customer-dedicated pool.
- I'll share a Calendar-invite.ics and a Drive folder with the prework and a short runbook for the load test. Please confirm the list of attendees who will join Zoom and who will be observer-only.
